headline: The head of Britain's domestic spy agency MI5 has warned that AI is already intensifying the contest between cyber attackers and defenders and could change the stakes on biological weapons.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an official on-record speech by a national security chief, though the bioweapons point is a warning about potential, not an incident.
importance_line: The head of the agency that tracks threats inside Britain naming AI as a growing security risk matters to the public first, then to the police and companies that defend against cyber attacks, but the bioweapons line is a warning about potential with no case described, and MI5 gives no figures on AI-assisted attacks.
summary: CNA reports that Ken McCallum, director general of MI5, Britain's domestic security service, said in the agency's annual threat briefing on Tuesday 13 Oct that AI is "already supercharging the cybersecurity contest between attackers and defenders" and has the "potential to change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons". He said MI5 has launched an AI Threat Assessment Centre this year at its London headquarters, has found suspects using AI to improve reconnaissance and attacks, including with AI-enabled drones, and that "human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are".
notes: Read from fulltext. No wire credit shown in the CNA text.
